summary: In this excerpt from Book 2, the narrator and Tresting meet Steve in a park, where Steve explains that their organization's existence must stay hidden from Pithica, which is near the Kiasma museum where Diana lives. Steve treats the narrator and Tresting as liabilities, yet is curious how the narrator walked away from Dawna Polk after learning she was not what she seemed. He offers to help them disappear and start new lives if they cooperate fully, and warns that they would reveal the group to Dawna Polk if they saw her again. Tresting responds with hostility, pointing out that the group usually just kills people.
one_line: In a tense park meeting, Steve offers the narrator and Tresting a hidden new life in exchange for full cooperation against Pithica.
key_facts: Steve says the only reason his group can exist is that Pithica does not know they do.
Steve states that the Kiasma museum is next to where Diana lives.
Steve says the group has managed its position against Pithica by taking swift and thorough measures against anyone who might reveal them.
Steve describes the narrator and Tresting as an obvious liability because they are targets of Pithica or have interacted with them.
The narrator's hand tightens on a weapon beneath the coat during the meeting, and the narrator believes they would win a fight but that killing Steve would mean nothing.
Steve finds it astounding and almost unbelievable that the narrator walked away from Dawna Polk knowing she was something other than what she presented.
Steve offers to help the narrator, Tresting and anyone else involved disappear and start a new life elsewhere if they cooperate fully, in all ways.
Steve says the disappearance would require removal entirely from civilization and constant oversight by his own people to prevent contact with Pithica.
Steve warns that if either of them sees Dawna Polk again, they will give the group away to her.
Steve says the offer to disappear is exceedingly generous and is not generally an opportunity the organization extends.
Tresting says, 'You usually just kill people, huh,' with the words crackling at the edges.
